scenes.headline: How one extra term turns SFT into preference training
scenes.sub: ORPO: an odds-ratio penalty, and no reference model.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Hyacinth! ORPO trains on preferred and rejected answers in a single run. Here's how its one extra term works.

scenes.text: SFT on chosen answers lifts the rejected ones too. ORPO adds one term that pushes the rejected response down, with no reference model.
scenes.say: The idea: fine-tuning on chosen answers lifts the rejected ones too. ORPO adds a term that pushes the rejected answer down, with no reference model.

scenes.title: The whole method
scenes.say: The whole method is one line.

parts.note: negative log-likelihood of the chosen response
parts.say: The usual SFT loss on the chosen answer. It never switches off.

parts.note: -log σ(log odds ratio, chosen over rejected)
parts.say: A penalty that shrinks as the chosen answer's odds rise above the rejected one's.

parts.note: its weight: 0.1 to 0.25 for the headline models
a geometric mean of per-token probabilities
parts.say: P is the average per-token probability, a geometric mean, not the whole sequence's probability.

parts.note: only matters while P sits between 0.1 and 0.9
parts.say: That keeps P where one minus P matters. For a whole sequence, the odds would just equal P.

scenes.title: Which ratio goes into the sigmoid?

left.title: Probability ratio, β 0.2
items: For loss 0.01, rejected must fall to 6.2e-11
left.say: With a probability ratio at beta point two, reaching a loss of point zero one means all but erasing the rejected answer.

right.title: Odds ratio
right.say: The odds ratio spreads over nine times wider, so the rejected answer only has to fall to about one and a half percent.

scenes.label: stronger pull on the rejected response when the model prefers it
scenes.note: 0.036 when the model is already right; 8.57 when wrong
scenes.say: The gradient has a gate. On pairs the model already gets right, ORPO is just SFT. When it prefers the rejected answer, the pull is two hundred and forty times stronger.

scenes.label: mean GSM8K change after ORPO, in SimPO's matched runs; DPO's is −8.27
scenes.say: And a result the paper never reported: in another group's matched runs, ORPO raised GSM8K math by two and a half points on average. DPO lost over eight.

scenes.text: Keep the SFT term live on every step, and preference training stops eating the model's arithmetic.

recap: SFT plus a log-odds-ratio penalty, no reference
Length-normalised P makes the odds ratio meaningful
The penalty only bites where the model is wrong
scenes.say: To recap: SFT plus an odds-ratio penalty, averaged per token, that only bites where the model is wrong.
